articles.title: Prem and RFU commit to expanding with English clubs after report of Welsh sides joining
articles.summary: Report claimed two Welsh sides could join Prem. Joint statement said ‘resources focused on English clubs’ Prem Rugby and the Rugby Football Union have stated they are committed to expanding the top flight with English clubs in response to a report claiming that two Welsh sides could soon join the…
body: According to the report, the Welsh Rugby Union is in advanced discussions with Prem Rugby and the RFU over the possibility of turning the Prem into a cross-border competition.

It comes as the WRU wrestles with a financial crisis that saw it announce a loss of £18.1m for 2025-26 last week, a figure that it says strengthens its case to reduce the number of regions from four to three.
The Prem is aiming to expand from 10 to 12 sides in time for the 2029-2030 season and English rugby’s governing bodies insist their priority is to back domestic teams.

“Resources are currently focused on supporting English clubs throughout the pyramid who aspire to join the league,” they said in a joint a statement. “The Prem is an attractive league and responsibility for its expansion sits with the Men’s Professional Rugby Board (MPRB), which has established detailed entry criteria that any prospective club would need to satisfy.”

articles.title: ‘This isn’t supposed to happen’: giant-slaying Fleetwood revels in fairytale Arsenal win
articles.summary: Fishing town in disbelief the morning after its footballing minnows beat mighty Arsenal on penalties. On a wet and windy night on the north-west coast of England, a League Two side sensationally knocked the Premier League champions out of the Carabao Cup.
body: Arsenal played at their iconic Highbury stadium until 2006, and Fleetwood’s ground has the same title, being named after Highbury Avenue, the adjoining street.

Fleetwood also play in red shirts with white sleeves in the style of the classic Arsenal kit. Nobody is exactly sure why, but according to Ray Curtis, a barman in the town’s King’s Arms: “Fleetwood’s first ever kit, the home kit, was given to them by Arsenal.”
And in the 2000s, not long after Patrick Vieira captained Arsenal, Fleetwood boasted a namesake star: a Brazilian striker called Magno Vieira.

At the 5,300-capacity Highbury on Wednesday morning, the floodlights that Fleetwood had hired for the occasion were being packed away. “It’s back to reality, back to being a League Two team, that’s our normal,” said Zsofia Wright, the ticket office and retail manager.

articles.title: Chiefs reportedly signing Tucker in wake of sexual misconduct allegations as Butker struggles
articles.summary: Tucker was banned under NFL’s conduct policy. Butker has missed five of 16 FG attempts this season. The Kansas City Chiefs are reportedly signing the former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad after Harrison Butker’s poor start to the season.
body: Tucker was widely considered one of the best kickers in NFL history until the Ravens released him in May 2025. The Ravens said his departure was a “football decision” after a slump in form, but the move came months after he was accused of inappropriate sexual behavior by massage therapists. Tucker denied the allegations and never faced criminal charges but he served a 10-game NFL ban for violating the league’s personal conduct policy.

More than a dozen massage therapists from spas and wellness centers in the Baltimore area accused Tucker of inappropriate sexual behavior. One therapist who spoke to the Baltimore Banner, which broke the story, described Tucker’s alleged behavior as “really degrading”. Another said: “I can’t watch sports anymore. I see his face everywhere.”

The 37-year-old has not played in the NFL since he was released by Baltimore. During his time with the Ravens, he made seven Pro Bowls and won the Super Bowl in his rookie season. His final season in Baltimore, in which he made just 73.3% of his field goals, was statistically the worst of his career. Tucker’s career average for field goals is 89.1%.

articles.title: London Broncos to go without £1.3m RFL funding if they enter Super League next year
articles.summary: Rugby Football League set to ratify elevation imminently. Partnership with NRL not expected now till 2028. London Broncos have agreed to a condition from the existing 14 Super League clubs that they must relinquish any rights to around £1.3m in central distribution funding if they are to enter the…
body: A partnership between Super League and Australia’s National Rugby League (NRL), which would mean the latter taking administrative control of the English game and injecting tens of millions of pounds of much-needed financial support, is now not expected to begin until 2028. Despite that, the expansion of Super League to 15 teams to include London has moved a step closer.

Many of the existing top-flight clubs were aware the NRL would insist on London’s inclusion in Super League when a partnership eventually starts. It was initially suspected that would be in 2027, but the two competitions have failed to agree a deal in time, though the NRL will assist in ensuring four Super League games per week are shown on Dazn next year.

That partnership not beginning until 2028 looked to have consigned London to another season in the Championship, which they won at a canter this year. But Super League clubs informed the Broncos they would still be willing to include them on the proviso they came in with zero distribution. The other 14 clubs currently get around £1.3m in central funding.

articles.title: BHA chief predicts 'devastating' impact on racing from Budget tax rise
articles.summary: British Horseracing Authority chief executive Brant Dunshea has warned the five per cent rise in machine gaming duty for betting shops announced in the Budget will have a “devastating impact” on the future of the sport.
body: Dunshea claimed racing should brace itself for a £57m hit to its finances with reductions in prize money, the loss of thousands of jobs and questions over the viability of racecourses moving forward.

"While the government has rejected a worst-case scenario to increase Machine Games Duty to 40 per cent, in raising the rate to 25 per cent it will nevertheless cause significant damage to racing's finances," Branshea said in a statement.
"There is now a clear risk that this decision will lead to the closure of hundreds, if not thousands, of betting shops across the country.

"British racing - which derives nearly a third of its £350m annual income from betting via high street shops - is now set to potentially lose £57m a year, based on the independent modelling that was shared with the Treasury ahead of today's Budget.

articles.title: Cheika happy to 'fly the flag' for Lebanon
articles.summary: Lebanon head coach Michael Cheika says he will be approaching the concluding fixture of his side's 2026 Rugby League World Cup campaign as if it is the final.
body: Having been involved in World Cup, Heineken Cup and Super Rugby finals in rugby union, an apparent dead-rubber fixture to conclude his side's involvement at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup may not initially seem to be among the most significant moments of Michael Cheika's storied coaching career.
However, the 59-year-old Australian says he will be treating Lebanon's meeting with France on Sunday (06:50 GMT) as if it were another final.

The Cedars, who reached the quarter-finals four years ago under Cheika, have been defeated by Papua New Guinea and Tonga in their opening two games, ending any hopes of reaching the knockout stages of this abridged tournament.
"We've got the one game here against France on Sunday and it's really our Grand Final," said the Australian, whose side did not have a fixture between this World Cup and the last.

articles.title: Marchant: England's selection policy tough for players outside Prem
articles.summary: Recalled England centre Joe Marchant admits the RFU selection policy which prohibits players being selected from outside of the Prem is tough for players abroad to deal with.
body: For three seasons between 2023/24 and 2025/26, Marchant - who has 28 caps - was ineligible to represent England due to playing with Stade Francais in France's Top 14.
The 30-year-old returned to Prem Rugby with Sale Sharks over the summer, and has since been included in England's squad ahead of November's Nations Championship.
However, players like Jack Willis at Toulouse, Tom Willis at Bordeaux and Kyle Sinckler at Toulon still cannot be picked.
"The whole time I was there, I wanted to be back playing for England," Marchant told Sky Sports. "We obviously know the rules, but I just wanted to be back in an England shirt.

articles.title: Ref Watch: Arsenal's red card appeal will fail - Dowman was aggressive
articles.summary: Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes Arsenal's appeal against Max Dowman's red card in their shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town will fail.
body: Dowman was sent off for violent conduct after kicking out at Harrison Neal following the defender's strong challenge on the teenager late in the fourth-round tie, which Arsenal lost on penalties.
Arsenal must submit appeal documents by 1pm on Thursday and are hopeful a decision will be made before their match at Liverpool, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

However, when asked if he thought Arsenal's appeal would be successful, Gallagher told Sky Sports News: "I don't, because of the aggressiveness of Dowman, and you can see the intent. I think it will fail."
He added: "I think it is [a red card]. People are comparing it to Cole Palmer on Saturday (with Mateus Fernandes), I think Dowman is a little bit more aggressive.

articles.title: How Mauricio Pochettino Broke Down Short-Sighted Barriers to Make the USMNT His Team
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has done something many USMNT fans and pundits never expected: he pulled the rug out from under them, challenged long-held assumptions, and reshaped the national team to reflect hi...
body: The United States men’s national team is officially Mauricio Pochettino’s. It took a little longer than many had hoped, but by the time the USMNT’s 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign came to an end, one thing had become clear: if Pochettino remained at the helm, significant changes were coming.

If the first four games of the new 2030 cycle have shown anything, it’s that the team is moving in a different direction. The USMNT won all four matches, three of them convincingly, delivering a run of results that made it feel like the program was finally building some genuine momentum again.

Pochettino introduced 13 new faces while giving opportunities to players who had previously faced heavy criticism from sections of the USMNT fanbase. Under the 54-year-old Argentine manager, the old ways of evaluating players and building this team look to be over.

An era built on cohesion, the right balance of ability and attitude, and, above all, what each player brings to the table has begun. Reputation, club affiliation, and preconceived notions are no longer supposed to dictate who belongs. Under Pochettino, the question is simpler: can you contribute to the team and buy into his vision?

“ Just being ready for the situation. These guys got us in the game, kept us in the game, and to come through, that spot feels good,” Williamson said, via Fox Sports. “It just shows the resiliency of this group. We continue to fight, and that’s been the motto of this series and this whole season. Just fight.”
